requirements.statement: Each use of a CSS image (background, background-image) to create the background colour of an element that can contain text is accompanied by a declaration of background colour (background, background-color), on the element or inherited from a parent.

citations.quote: chaque utilisation d’une image pour créer une couleur de fond d’un élément susceptible de contenir du texte, via CSS (`background`, `background-image`), est-elle accompagnée d’une déclaration de couleur de fond (`background`, `background-color`), au moins, héritée d’un parent ?

routes.statement: A background colour is declared on the element or on one of its ancestors.

citations.quote: accompagnée d’une déclaration de couleur de fond (`background`, `background-color`), au moins, héritée d’un parent

routes.statement: The text remains legible when the background image is absent.

citations.quote: Déterminer l’élément qui contient le texte et vérifier que si l’image d’arrière-plan est absente, le texte reste lisible ;
Si c’est le cas, **le test est validé**.

rationale.text: The wording asks that a CSS image used to create the background colour of an element that can contain text be accompanied by a declared background colour. The methodology checks something else: that the text stays legible when the background image is absent, and validates the test in that case. Both are listed as routes, since a page that meets either could be judged to pass, and a missed route would make the tool fail a correct page. Two judgments block any claim. Whether an image is used to create a background colour, rather than to show a picture, a pattern, an icon or a decoration, is judgment; a gradient is an image in CSS and may or may not count. Whether text stays legible without the image is judgment too. A text over a CSS background image with no background colour declared anywhere fails the first route, but it may pass the second, for example dark text on the default light canvas, and legibility is not something code decides with certainty. No check can fault under every reading, so the entry is none. No axe rule is tagged. Applicability is judgment: whether a page uses an image to create a background colour is judgment. Needs is empty.
